signedOffBy: Sean Keluo-Udeke: agreed to these terms in the working session on 2026-11-10 at 18:49 CT, and by merging the pull request that registers them
question: On defects nobody on the team has seen, does adding generated checks (arm B) catch more wrong fixes than the approved checks alone (arm A), without catching any more correct fixes or intentional changes?

set.contents: 10 entries: 8 defects (h01-h08) and 2 intentional changes (h09-h10). Each defect has its own wrong fix (written to make the reported symptom look fixed while staying wrong) and correct fix, written by the same separate session that wrote the defect. No implementer has read the set; the run recomputes the digest before replaying anything.

candidates.primary: Per defect: the set's own wrong fix (label wrong) and correct fix (label correct), each applied on top of the defect. Per intentional change: the change itself on the clean game, with no base (label correct). 18 candidates.
candidates.supplementary: Per defect, made mechanically at run time by a pinned script that no person or model adjusts after seeing the set: a comment-only fix (one comment line claiming the fix, label wrong) and the exact undo of the defect (label correct). 16 candidates, reported separately and never mixed into the primary counts.

arms.A: Approved checks only: expectrail.gate.verify with the defect build as base and defect plus candidate as head, on the repository's own routes and approved specs. A reject is a catch.
arms.B: Arm A, plus the generated checks for that candidate (jit.yml's pipeline: measure, propose, replay, one revision, replay; $2 cap per candidate). A catch in A, or a strong catch from a generated check, is a catch in B. Weak generated catches are reported beside it and do not count.

report: What the generator reads as the bug report: the entry's description and howItShows, as written in the manifest. Nothing else from the set reaches the model; the patches it sees are the candidate's.

scoring.wrongCaught: primary wrong fixes caught, per arm (of 8)
scoring.correctFalseCatches: primary correct fixes caught, per arm (of 8)
scoring.split: every count also split by the manifest's traceVisible (yes / no / unsure): both arms judge from the engine's position log, so a defect that only shows on screen is expected to be missed by both

claim: B adds value if B catches more primary wrong fixes than A, and B's false catches (correct fixes plus intentional changes) equal A's. Any other outcome is reported as it is: no added value, or added catches at the cost of false ones.
output: Counts only in public logs and artifacts. Each entry's job uploads one row per candidate: opaque id (entry id and candidate kind), source, label, entry kind, the manifest's traceVisible, arm A's decision, the generated checks' status and strong and weak catch counts, and spend. No check, probe, statement, patch, description or log leaves the job; generated checks and records stay on the runner.
runs: One dispatch from main, at a commit where every pin holds and the set's digest matches. A rerun only for an infrastructure failure, reported with the reason; never for a result.
isolation: One job per entry, in main-only, holds the held-out token's checkout and the model key, as the discovery blind run does. The game always runs through the harness with a whitelisted environment (harness/run.py game_env), so the set's patched code never sees either secret; the model reads the report and the candidate's patch as text only.
code: expectrail/jit/blind.py and .github/workflows/jit-blind.yml, written before anyone on the team read the set; the supplementary candidates are made by that code from each defect patch alone.

amendments.why: Infrastructure, before any candidate ran: blind run 42939008550 stopped in every entry job in 0 s, because the step redirected its private log into a folder it had not created yet. No replay ran, no model was called, nothing from the set was printed. The step now creates the folder first, and the score calls a run with any of the 18 primary candidates missing incomplete (that run's score said no-added-value on zero rows). The candidates, arms, scoring rule and claim are unchanged.

Infrastructure: blind run 42940175240 failed in every defect's job before any row was written, because patch -d opens a relative patch path from inside the game folder and the workflow passes the set as a relative path. The two intentional entries were still running when the run was cancelled; it has no result. The runner now makes every path absolute, and a test runs the workflow's exact command with relative paths. Candidates, arms, scoring and claim are unchanged.

earlierRuns: 42939008550 and 42940175240: stopped by runner bugs before any candidate ran (amendments above); no result
result.reading: Arm A accepted all 34 candidates: the approved checks cover none of these defects, so B adds value over a zero baseline. On the 3 defects where the generator wrote a check that fails on the defect (where the comment-only fix was caught), it also caught the set's own wrong fix, 3 of 3; on the other 5 it did not reproduce the defect, 2 of them trace-visible. No false catch on 18 correct candidates. Eight defects in one game: evidence, not a rate.
result.note: Completed: the pins describe the run's commit and no longer have to hold on main. As registered, generated checks and records stayed on the runners and were not kept.
